Under the agreement, Hertz’s newly launched unit, Oro Mobility, will manage vehicle operations for Uber, including maintenance, charging, cleaning and logistics for autonomous vehicles. original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, how AI is playing a part. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!

I am back from vacation. What did I miss? Turns out, quite a lot — including the end of the Uber-Waymo partnership in Phoenix. Uber and Waymo still have robotaxi service partnerships in Atlanta and Austin. The question is not if, but when will these agreements end? But that isn’t the most intriguing question, in my opinion. I am far more intrigued by how these two companies will behave once the remaining partnerships end.

---

[Lähde: Fox Business]
FOX Business' Taylor Riggs reports Uber and Hertz are expanding their partnership to power robotaxis, with Hertz naming Uber as its first major partner in a push to reshape the future of mobility.

Hertz is expanding beyond its traditional car rental business through a new partnership with Uber aimed at powering both autonomous robotaxi fleets and driver-led rideshare operations, signaling a broader shift in the transportation industry.

Under the agreement, Hertz’s newly launched unit, Oro Mobility, will manage vehicle operations for Uber, including maintenance, charging, cleaning and logistics for autonomous vehicles.

The robotaxi service, which will use Lucid vehicles equipped with Nuro self-driving technology, is expected to launch in the San Francisco Bay Area later this year, with potential "expansion opportunities" in 2027.

Hertz will also supply and operate fleets of vehicles driven by its own employees on Uber’s platform, building on a pilot program that has already expanded into Los Angeles and San Francisco with additional markets planned.

UBER, RIVIAN INK $1.25B DEAL TO PUT THOUSANDS OF ROBOTAXIS ON US STREETS

A Lucid Gravity autonomous taxi at the first National AV Safety Forum held by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration at the Department of Transportation headquarters in Washington, D.C., March 10, 2026. (Alex Kent/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The partnership highlights a shift in the ridesharing model away from individual car ownership toward centrally managed fleets. Hertz is positioning itself as a transportation infrastructure provider, leveraging its expertise in large-scale vehicle logistics and maintenance.

Uber, meanwhile, is continuing to emphasize a platform-driven model, relying on partners like Hertz to manage fleet operations as it scales both human-driven and autonomous rides.

For Hertz, the deal represents a high-stakes bet on a new growth strategy after years of turbulence, while, for Uber, it marks another step toward a hybrid network that could eventually integrate human drivers with self-driving vehicles at scale.

Uber is continuing to emphasize a platform-driven model. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO

"Partnering with Hertz’s Oro Mobility will help us continue to bring the best autonomous technology onto the Uber platform and accelerate the transition to a hybrid network in which both driver-led and autonomous rideshare operations can scale and serve comm

---

[Lähde: Carscoops]
The robotaxi wars are heating up as Mobileye has announced plans to launch its own autonomous ride-hailing business. This is an interesting development as the company is making the jump from supplier to fleet operator.

Mobileye says it will launch a robotaxi service in a “major metropolitan U.S. market” next year. The company aims to have an initial fleet of approximately 100 vehicles and an illustration suggests they’ll be crossovers equipped with a roof-mounted sensor pod as well as sensors in the front and rear fenders.

More: VW’s MQB Lineup Getting New Level 2+ Autonomous Driving Tech From Mobileye

The company will apparently take a cautious approach to “validate the operational model under fully driverless conditions.” If the initial rollout is a success, Mobileye plans to deploy approximately 17,000 robotaxis over the following five years.

While there are more questions than answers at this point, the robotaxi will use Mobileye Drive as well as Moovit’s Mobility Platform. They’ll be joined by “consumer-facing applications, multi-modal trip planning, AV mission control, fleet-management technologies, and integration with teleoperation infrastructure.”

Mobileye CEO Amnon Shashua said, “As interest in autonomous mobility accelerates, the industry has become increasingly dependent on a small number of technology providers and business models. We believe there is an opportunity for a new approach – one built on deep autonomous-driving expertise, strong industry partnerships, and proven capabilities across the mobility ecosystem.”

The company said it remains committed to supplying Mobileye Drive to automakers, mobility operators, and other customers even though they’re launching their own robotaxi service. They added the effort provides a “complementary path to market that can accelerate deployment, generate operational learnings, and further demonstrate the capabilities of the Mobileye Drive platform at scale.”

Additional information will be released at a Capital Markets Day event later this year, but Mobileye said they’ll be working with “AV-ready vehicle platform manufacturers.” This suggests their upcoming robotaxi will be based on an existing off-the-shelf vehicle.

While Ford and GM have thrown in the towel on robotaxis, there’s no shortage of competition from Tesla, Amazon’s Zoox, and Google’s Waymo. Uber is also betting big on robotaxis and has plans for up to 50,000 models based on the Rivian R2 as well as others built on the Lucid Gravity.

payload.title: Uber järjestelee robottaksikumppanuuksiaan uudelleen – Hertz ottaa vastuulleen ajoneuvojen ylläpidon
payload.summary: Uberin ja Waymon yhteistyö on päättynyt Phoenixissa, mutta jatkuu Atlantassa ja Austinissa. Samalla Uber laajentaa yhteistyötään Hertzin kanssa rakentaakseen ihmiskuljettajia ja robottakseja yhdistävää verkostoa.
payload.content:
Uberin robottaksiverkosto on muutoksessa: yhtiön yhteistyö Waymon kanssa on päättynyt Phoenixissa, vaikka kumppanusten yhteiset palvelut jatkuvat Atlantassa ja Austinissa. Samalla Uber syventää yhteistyötään autovuokraamo Hertzin kanssa ja valmistelee uuden autonomisen kyytipalvelun käynnistämistä San Franciscon lahden alueella myöhemmin vuonna 2026.

## Waymo-yhteistyö jatkuu kahdessa kaupungissa

Uber ja Waymo tarjoavat edelleen yhteisiä robottaksipalveluja Atlantassa ja Austinissa. Phoenixissa yhteistyö on kuitenkin päättynyt. Saatavilla olevissa tiedoissa ei kerrota, milloin tai millä ehdoilla Phoenixia koskenut järjestely päättyi, eikä Atlanta- ja Austin-yhteistyön mahdolliselle päättymiselle ole ilmoitettu aikataulua.

Phoenixin muutos nostaa esiin kysymyksen siitä, miten Uber ja Waymo toimisivat jäljellä olevien sopimusten päätyttyä. TechCrunchin mukaan kiinnostava kysymys ei koske vain sopimusten mahdollista päättymisajankohtaa, vaan myös yhtiöiden toimintaa sen jälkeen. Uberin muut kumppanuudet osoittavat, että yhtiö rakentaa robottaksitarjontaansa useiden teknologia- ja ajoneuvotoimittajien varaan.

## Hertz hoitaa ajoneuvojen käytännön toiminnan

Hertz laajenee yhteistyön kautta perinteisen autonvuokrauksen ulkopuolelle. Yhtiön uusi Oro Mobility -yksikkö ryhtyy hallinnoimaan Uberin ajoneuvojen käytännön toimintoja. Sen tehtäviin kuuluvat autonomisten autojen huolto, lataaminen, puhdistaminen ja logistiikka. Hertz on nimennyt Uberin uuden yksikkönsä ensimmäiseksi merkittäväksi kumppaniksi.

San Franciscon lahden alueelle suunnitellussa robottaksipalvelussa käytetään Lucidin valmistamia ajoneuvoja, joissa on Nuron itseajavaa teknologiaa. Palvelun odotetaan käynnistyvän myöhemmin vuonna 2026. Sopimukseen liittyy myös mahdollisuus toiminnan laajentamiseen vuonna 2027, mutta lähdeaineistossa ei yksilöidä mahdollisia uusia alueita tai tarkempaa aikataulua.

## Uber tavoittelee hybridiverkostoa

Järjestely tukee Uberin alustapohjaista mallia, jossa kumppanit vastaavat ajoneuvokannan toiminnasta ja teknologiasta Uberin tarjotessa kyytialustan. Yhtiö pyrkii kasvattamaan sekä ihmiskuljettajien hoitamia kyytejä että autonomisia palveluja. Tavoitteena on hybridiverkosto, jossa kuljettajien käyttämät autot ja robottaksit voivat palvella asiakkaita rinnakkain ja laajentua samanaikaisesti.

Hertzille sopimus merkitsee uutta kasvuhanketta yhtiön perinteisen liiketoiminnan rinnalle. Uberille se tarjoaa tavan lisätä autonomisia ajoneuvoja alustalleen kumppanin hoitaessa niiden päivittäisen ylläpidon. Kumppanuuden merkitys korostuu samalla, kun Uberin ja Waymon yhteistyörakenne on jo muuttunut Phoenixissa mutta jatkuu toistaiseksi kahdella muulla markkina-alueella.
summary_bullets: Uberin ja Waymon robottaksiyhteistyö on päättynyt Phoenixissa mutta jatkuu Atlantassa ja Austinissa.
Hertzin Oro Mobility vastaa Uberin autonomisten ajoneuvojen huollosta, lataamisesta, puhdistamisesta ja logistiikasta.
Lucidin ajoneuvoihin ja Nuron teknologiaan perustuva palvelu on tarkoitus käynnistää San Franciscon lahden alueella myöhemmin vuonna 2026.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli erottaa vahvistetut kumppanuusmuutokset tulevaisuutta koskevista avoimista kysymyksistä. Atlanta- ja Austin-sopimusten päättymisestä tai aikataulusta ei ole vahvistettua tietoa.

FOX Business' Taylor Riggs reports Uber and Hertz are expanding their partnership to power robotaxis, with Hertz naming Uber as its first major partner in a push to reshape the future of mobility. Hertz is expanding beyond its traditional car rental business through a new partnership with Uber aimed at powering both autonomous robotaxi fleets and driver-led rideshare operations, signaling a broader shift in the transportation industry. Under the agreement, Hertz’s newly launched unit, Oro Mobility, will manage vehicle operations for Uber, including maintenance, charging, cleaning and logistics for autonomous vehicles. The robotaxi service, which will use Lucid vehicles equipped with Nuro self-driving technology, is expected to launch in the San Francisco Bay Area later this year, with potential "expansion opportunities" in 2027.

Uber, meanwhile, is continuing to emphasize a platform-driven model, relying on partners like Hertz to manage fleet operations as it scales both human-driven and autonomous rides. For Hertz, the deal represents a high-stakes bet on a new growth strategy after years of turbulence, while, for Uber, it marks another step toward a hybrid network that could eventually integrate human drivers with self-driving vehicles at scale.
